title: Bounded world ticks and ecology failure modes
summary: Use compact state, finite action tables and inspectable event history. Proposed caps are design defaults, not measured throughput. NPC and intervention principals remain separate; neither can force a quest, consent, Fate action or anomaly.

sources.title: Stars Without Number Revised, Free Edition
sources.locator: Printed pp.211–214: Using Factions; Faction Turn; Acting During A Turn

sources.title: Dwarf Fortress development: Legends and World Chronicle
Did players destroy the UO ecology?

claims.statement: Blades clocks summarize fictional progress, while SWN uses selective faction turns and typically one action type per faction per turn. Neither requires continuous simulation of every actor.
Dwarf Fortress development notes describe accumulated historical entries and linked navigation. They support inspectable history, not proof of an ARGO-compatible replay algorithm.

Koster’s firsthand retrospective says ecology AI was removed during beta because of search/pathfinding cost, and separately describes finite-resource hoarding blocking replenishment. He disputes popular retellings. Launch-week extinction is not established here.

proposals.title: Bounded deterministic background tick policy

fields.name: authorized_target_tick
fields.meaning: Explicit advance request; no wall-clock default

fields.name: draw_slot
fields.meaning: Seed remains private; caller cannot fish by retry ID

rules: At most8ticks per invocation,16active entities,4projects per entity,64evaluated candidates per tick and32effect entries. Reject oversized configurations rather than silently dropping actors.
Canonical ID order; finite prerequisite/resource rules; one action per entity per tick. Waiting is valid. No LLM call required.
Authority derives draw slots from scope/ruleset/tick/entity/project/slot, never retry IDs or invocation chunking; this changes current RNG semantics and needs migration.
Validate all effects under the writer lock and head check, then commit the complete tick atomically or reject it.
Completion may produce one bounded follow-up candidate eligible next tick, never an immediate recursive cascade. Resume remaining authorized backlog only through another bounded call.

benchmarks.title: Wall-clock isolation
benchmarks.given: World is at10 with no authorized advance.
then: World time, canonical projection and head are unchanged.

benchmarks.title: Chunk-independent catch-up
benchmarks.given: Explicit target20 from10 with a fixed seed.
then: Same physical state and per-tick random commitments.
No skipped ticks; retries append no duplicate effects.
benchmarks.oracle: Canonical graph/state comparison; full event hashes need identical message identities too.

benchmarks.title: No completion cascade
then: One completion and zero remaining resource.
Follow-up cannot execute before next tick.
benchmarks.oracle: Effect counts, resource invariants and unchanged state on rejected tick.

open_questions: SWN primary book was inspected on a third-party mirror; official storefront returned403. Pin the final distributed edition before encoding detailed rules.
UO testimony is retrospective and contested, not contemporaneous telemetry.
No background tick action, resource ecology or physical graph projection is implemented by this starter research.
